findings: Over-refusal of read forms: a multi-purpose verb carrying a modifier outside its declared read union exits 97 instead of forwarding. Measured through the shim at head against a foreign repository: reflog show --oneline -1 rc=97, stash list --oneline refused, worktree list --porcelain refused. This is deliberate deny-by-default and recoverable by rewriting the invocation, but it narrows the followup's otherwise execs the real git unchanged.

Rationale overstatement: the comment in reckon/worker_git_shim.py and the manifest account state that abbreviated --output spellings reach the same write because git resolves any unambiguous long-option prefix. Measured on this host's git 2.39.3, log, diff and show reject --outp=, --outpu= and --out= as unrecognized or ambiguous, so those spellings never reach a write here; the refusal remains correct and conservative, and the 3-character floor is safe because 2-character prefixes are rejected too. The prefix logic still closes a real class: the describe synonyms --di, --dirt and --dirty DO resolve in real git and DO move a stale foreign index when run directly, and the shipped isolation covers them.

Residual: when the private index copy cannot be made, the forward falls back to a plain invocation. Optional locks are still off on that path, but a refreshing read could then write the target's index. Narrow, and not exercised by the shipped suite.
Residual, outside the node's declared property: a target repository's own config naming external programs (diff textconv, core.fsmonitor) can execute them during a forwarded foreign read.
